title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs', a figure F carries a poset F~ of its 'cells' or pieces. Two relations appear: F' ≤ F (sub-figure) and F' ≪ F (refinement). Sub-figures of F correspond to a class of subsets of F~, written Pf(F~). These are most plausibly down-closed ('closed') subsets, i.e. closed sets of the Alexandrov topology on F~. A refinement F' ≪ F gives a canonical monotone map φ: F'~ → F~. It sends a cell X' of F' to the unique cell X of F with X' °≪ X ('carrier map').

Previous page. For a sub-figure G ≤ F, the induced refinement G' of G is defined as an Inf, with respect to ≪, of F' and G. Page 65 checks that this is a genuine Inf. It reduces to points Z ∈ M (axiom At 4) and to a lemma using At 7.

This page.
- Corollary 1. If F' is itself a sub-figure (F' ≤ F), then G' is a sub-figure of G, hence of F, and equals the intersection sub-figure F'∧G. The proof is formal: exchange the roles of F' and G, and read off the identification G' = F'∧G from (I.60).
- Notation: G' =: F'.G.
- Corollary 2 (1.61). For F' ≪ F, the map Sousfig(F) → Sousfig(F'), G ↦ F'.G, commutes with Sup and Inf. Proof: under the identifications Sousfig(F) = Pf(F~) and Sousfig(F') = Pf(F'~), this map is φ* = φ^{-1}. Inverse image under a monotone (Alexandrov-continuous) map preserves arbitrary unions and intersections of down-sets.
- Notation: ∨F_i for the Sup of sub-figures.
- Corollary 3 (begun here, finished on p. 67). Take F' ≪ F and a covering F = Sup F_i by sub-figures, with F_ij = F_i ∧ F_j. Let F'_i, F'_ij be the induced refinements. Then F'_i ∧ F'_j = F'_ij, the family is compatible on overlaps, and F' = Sup F'_i.

Purpose. This prepares a gluing ('recollement') principle for refinements. On p. 67 it is made into the axiom AR: refinements of the cells X ∈ F~ that are compatible under restriction glue to a refinement of F. In effect, refinements form a sheaf over the face poset. The whole serves Grothendieck's axiomatization of 'tame' (modérée) topology: polyhedra and stratified figures together with their subdivisions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Corollary 2 rests on the identification Sousfig(F) ≅ Pf(F~) and on φ being monotone, so that φ^{-1} of a closed (down-closed) set is again closed. Both are assumed, presumably established in earlier pages (I.60 etc.).

Corollary 1 is stated under 'F' ≤ F' while the surrounding construction assumes F' ≪ F. It implicitly uses that a sub-figure counts as a (degenerate) refinement, or that F.G makes sense for F' ≤ F. This is presumably covered by the axioms but is not spelled out here.

ideas.what: Restricting a refinement (subdivision) F' of F to a sub-figure G, defined as an infimum F'.G
ideas.modern_name: Induced subdivision of a subcomplex / restriction of a subdivision
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs notes (cote 156); tame topology is programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5

ideas.what: Sub-figures identified with closed (down-closed) subsets of the cell poset F~; refinement induces a monotone carrier map φ, and restriction becomes φ^{-1}, a lattice homomorphism preserving all Sup and Inf
ideas.modern_name: Carrier map of a subdivision; continuous map of finite T0 (Alexandrov) spaces; inverse image as a frame/complete-lattice homomorphism

ideas.what: Gluing principle for refinements over a covering by sub-figures, leading to the axiom AR on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf condition for subdivisions over the face poset (cellular sheaf / sheaf on an Alexandrov space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cellular sheaves: Shepard (1985), Curry (2014); classical PL gluing of subdivisions

missed.claim: This page is part of an axiomatic system (axioms At 1–7, AR) for 'figures' and their refinements. It aims at a foundation of tame topology in which subdivisions form a sheaf over the cell poset. The program was not published or developed by others in this form; o-minimality (van den Dries) and later work took different routes.
missed.quote: ça donne un principe de recollement pour les raffinements de F (p.67); Corollaire 2 ... commute aux Sup et aux Inf
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with combinatorial/poset models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, cellular sheaves). Treating 'refinements as a sheaf on the Alexandrov space of cells' is a natural axiom for tame geometry that is not standard in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The content of this page is routine lattice theory: inverse image along a carrier map preserves Sup and Inf. Its interest lies only in being part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame-topology program, whose gluing axiom AR appears on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'sous-figure de G, [?] de F' is likely 'sous-figure de G, donc de F'.
'd'un ordonné' is probably 'd'ensembles ordonnés' (canonical maps of ordered sets).
'Pf' is probably an abbreviation for the set of closed/final parts ('parties fermées') of the poset; the last words before it ('au sens [?] [?]') are illegible in the image.
'Notation F'.G' and 'Notation ∨F_i' are left-margin annotations, not part of the main text.
In Corollary 1, the struck-out text was a first attempt '(1.61) G' = Inf^ε(F', G)', replaced by the statement about F' ≤ F.
